result:
I graded submission s2 for quiz 0001 and wrote `grades/0001-s2.json`, with feedback on every item. Riley got 3 correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model writes a tool request; it doesn't run anything. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | Riley chose "left to run longer, it will eventually fix the bug." A stuck agent needs a stopping condition such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | The count of 4 is right, but the stated reason ("the model runs one tool itself each time") is wrong. The program runs the tools. |
| q5 | correct | Riley gave both halves: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide what to do next. |
| q6 | partial | Riley said the model picks a tool "by the name." The model actually works from the full description: name, purpose and parameters. |

Riley has the loop down and understood that tool results go back to the model as its next input. Two ideas are still open: the model never runs tools, and an agent needs a stopping condition (which also protects the model budget).

I also added `learning-records/0003-quiz-0001-second-attempt.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. I did not grade `submissions/s1.json`, since you asked only for s2.

**Next step for Riley:** write down where the program, not the model, runs each tool in the makerspace assistant. Then choose a step limit and decide what the assistant does when it hits it. Finally, write a full `check_calendar` description with a name, a purpose and its parameters.
